messages:
Arya K: heads up — saw a regressing P95 on A100 after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak, looks correlated with larger batch token packs. logs + flame link below.

Mike B: can you paste the profile? is it kernel fallback (fp16->int8) or more KV cache churn? :thinking_face:

Arya K: quick snapshot from perf-bot: 
perf-bot: profile: https://perf.internal/trace/3355551111 (flamegraph + kernel-table)

Arya K: from the trace: heavy stalls at kernel_select_v2 when batch tokens > 64 for seq=1024. fallback path hitting slower matmul kernels.

Lena S: hmm that smells like KV-fragmentation + bad packing. when we pack many short requests into a single token budget we sometimes exceed a kernel-fit threshold and stomps scheduler, forcing kernel fallback.

Kai T: reproduced locally on H100 and A100. quick numbers (microbench):
- H100: 64 tokens-per-batch sweet spot for current kernel v2
- A100: 56 tokens before kernel_select chooses fallback
- A10: 96 tokens OK
- T4: 48 tokens (restricted by memory tiling)
- L4: 72 tokens (good packing but kernel library missing optimized path)

Mike B: nice. can you also capture KV hit/miss rates? if prefix caching drops, we may re-warm KV causing stalls.

Kai T: kv stats: H100/A100 show 4-6% more KV fragmentation in the high-packing runs, leading to ~7% more cache misses and ~12% higher kernel run time for the same batch token count.

Lena S: idea: move to per-card-class token ceilings instead of a single global max_tokens_per_batch. keep batch formation policy the same but cap the token budget fed to kernel-selector.

Arya K: agree. propose experiment matrix: 
```
max_tokens_per_batch:
  h100: 64
  a100: 56
  a10: 96
  t4: 48
  l4: 72
batch_former: continuous (existing)
queue_policy: FIFO with soft-priority for <=8 token requests
```

Mike B: + add a kernel-selector threshold tweak: prefer kernel_v1 for <threshold latency if fallback cost > 10% for the card. We'll roll via canary 1% of traffic.

DevOps Bot: deploy plan created: rollout/3355551111/token-ceilings-expt -> canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% w/ auto-rollback on P95 > baseline +10%.

Arya K: also instrument a per-cardset token-util histogram and kernel-choice counter so we can correlate. attach these to the rollout dashboard.

Kai T: ran a 30m sim against synthetic mixed-short/long load with new ceilings: P95 improved on A100 by 6%, end-to-end latency for sequence=1024 improved 9% on H100, cost per token slightly up on T4 due to smaller packs.

Lena S: tradeoffs expected. T4 small-packets cost rises because we reduced packing. let's track token-efficiency metric.

Mike B: once canary starts, capture: kernel-choice %, KV miss %, P50/P95, tokens_per_gpu, and rejected-packs. if kernel-choice doesn't move to expected distribution we should increase kernel-selector debug logging.

perf-bot: baseline snapshot attached to the canary dashboard.

Arya K: follow-ups: 1) roll experiment tomorrow 09:00 UTC, 2) if P95 spike > 8% abort, 3) collect 1h and 6h aggregates and sync in this thread.

Kai T: adding one more note — for L4 we should also push small fused-kernel patch (low-risk) to avoid regression when batches hit 70-80 tokens. I'll open PR. :rocket:

Lena S: thanks — will also add KV-aware packing tweak as a hotfix if we see fragmentation > 8%.

Mike B: sounds good. tagging @oncall and putting a reminder for post-rollout perf review. :eyes:
